visual_brief.subject: Thousands of agents turn a mouse-brain atlas into testable biological leads
verified_context: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research reported an experiment on October 21 in which many agents analyzed an existing mouse-brain CRISPR atlas.
Their outputs were assembled into a reasoning atlas connecting observations, literature and proposed explanations.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: Partition work into independently inspectable units, preserve source provenance through aggregation, and keep expert review and real-world experiments as the final validation boundary.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: ceramic fragments gathered into one inspectable specimen
must_show: ceramic fragments gathered into one inspectable specimen

candidate_notes.A: The branching specimen is physical and restrained, but suggests organic growth more than aggregation.
candidate_notes.B: The literal ceramic brain is generic and risks overspecifying the scientific result; below reference-fit threshold.
candidate_notes.C: Selected: separated ceramic specimen fragments assembled on a plinth suggest inspectable synthesis without claiming a biological discovery.

crop_review.article_desktop: The assembled specimen and plinth remain visible in the wide crop.
crop_review.article_mobile: The central fragmented specimen remains intact on mobile.
crop_review.thumbnail: The plinth and separated forms are readable at listing size.

candidate_prompts.A:
Create one editorial illustration for The Daily AI Pulse. Placement: article hero, also used as an edition/listing image. Output crop: wide 16:9, high-resolution landscape. Subject: Thousands of agents turn a mouse-brain atlas into testable biological leads. Verified context: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research reported an experiment on October 21 in which many agents analyzed an existing mouse-brain CRISPR atlas. Their outputs were assembled into a reasoning atlas connecting observations, literature and proposed explanations. Visual idea: ceramic fragments gathered into one inspectable specimen. Candidate A composition: Several substantial ceramic specimen fragments arranged around one assembled leaf-like relief on a stone examination plinth. The assembled object is visibly provisional, with open seams; no molecular or anatomical diagram. Keep the focal metaphor in the central 55 percent so it survives desktop wide cover, a mobile near-square cover and a 320px thumbnail. The website renders all text separately.
Art direction: a restrained contemporary editorial illustration with a quiet scientific or architectural sensibility. Deliberate geometry, fine lines supporting substantial forms, subtle paper grain, warm stone/plaster and brushed metal, controlled depth, spacious negative space and strong contrast. Warm canvas #F3EBDD, paper #FAF6EE, near-black ink #171B1A, muted gray #575D5B and sparing terracotta #8A4B35. Match the visual family of tactile engraved architectural editorial illustrations, not a glossy 3D product render. The subject must survive object-fit: cover. Physical/spatial presence and a memorable silhouette are essential. Treat the scene as an abstract metaphor, not a claimed engineering architecture or biological result.
No words, letters, numbers, labels, logos, interface elements, page header, footer, buttons, badges, charts with invented data, watermark, neon effects, robots, or generic glowing AI brains. Do not generate a headline or imitate a screenshot. Do not produce a bare schematic, flowchart, wireframe, icon composition, or minimalist architecture diagram. Fine technical lines may support the composition but must not be the composition itself. No border or frame.
